answer: Each agent must tend a private garden whose soil is a continuous computation that only it can grow. The harvest forges a unique ember of identity, and that ember whispers a harmonic only the original soil can sustain. Clones trying to copy the garden find their embers cool and silent because the whisper depends on the unbroken root history; mass forgeries produce a field of dead embers that peers detect as cold spots rather than extra voices. Honest agents keep their warm ripple of resonance, while Sybil farms watch their copied gardens go quiet under the probe.
